Hi Tessa —

Thanks for sending. Quick answers:
- SOC 2 Type II attestation period ends 2027-11 (we can provide the report and the complimentary mapping).
- Pen-test: HV prefers late July for a full blackbox window but can be flexible to accommodate Redwood's constraints. We generally expect a 14-day notice, not 30.
- Evidence cadence: we like a short cadence pre-test (two weekly snapshots) and a final package afterwards.

A couple of asks from our side before we accept language:
1) Can Redwood supply a scoped list of evidence items (hostnames, logs types, retention windows)?
2) What secure transfer mechanisms do you support for evidence (SFTP, presigned S3, encrypted SCP)?
3) Clarify whether "inspection rights" in the exhibit require physical on-site access or allow virtual/agent-based assessment.

I've attached our internal pen-test policy that outlines HV expectations (HV_pen_test_policy.pdf). Happy to hop on a focused 30-min sync with Karthik + Laura tomorrow if that helps.

Best,
Elena Morales
Director, Information Security — HealthVantage

Elena / team —

Thanks for the details. I reviewed the draft exhibit and HV's pen-test policy. Below is proposed language we can insert as a focused paragraph in the Security Exhibit to address inspection/pen-test and evidence cadence. This is intentionally short so it can be copy/pasted into the MSA/order form: 

--- proposed redline (suggested) ---
"Inspection & Penetration Testing: Customer may conduct or commission non-destructive penetration testing of the Services provided by Redwood subject to the following conditions: (a) Customer will provide Redwood with at least fourteen (14) calendar days' prior written notice describing the scope, objectives, and proposed testing window; (b) testing shall be limited to non-destructive, application-layer, and network-layer techniques expressly agreed to in advance; (c) any on-site activity requires mutual scheduling and a written scope addendum; (d) Redwood will provide a pre-test evidence package consisting of two (2) weekly snapshot exports and a post-test evidence bundle within ten (10) business days of test completion; and (e) the parties will follow the escalation path in which Customer notifies Redwood Security, Redwood provides a 24-hour initial acknowledgement and an operational plan within 3 business days to remediate or isolate findings."
--- end suggested redline ---

Notes and clarifications:
- We need to preserve Redwood's obligation boundaries: Redwood will not accept language that implies unlimited access to production or full source-level inspections.
- Evidence transfer: Redwood prefers presigned S3 URLs (encrypted transport) for large log bundles; we can also provide an SFTP endpoint if HV requires it.
- For the SOC2 mapping: Laura, can you confirm the standard export package (fields and retention) so I can reference it in the redline?

If HV is comfortable with the 14-day notice and the presigned S3 approach I can incorporate this language into the MSA redline and send a single packet for signature. Otherwise, propose specifics and we will iterate.

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
